text.p: - One of Moscow's official power structures, likely to have created the Russian Fund for Invalids of the War in Afghanistan several years ago, could be behind the mass murder of its leaders on Sunday.
- By granting tax-breaks to different social structures which the state finds itself unable to support, the government contributes to further criminalisation of the country's economy.

- The French government, having confiscated Russia's property and accounts in France after the 1917 Bolshevik revolution, did not use them to reimburse the Russian loan holders and is no less responsible for their misfortunes than the Russian government itself.
- Tensions mount in Russia's Defence Council as Defence Minister Igor Rodionov is reluctant to go ahead with army reform.
- The speed of President Boris Yeltsin's recovery surprises his doctors.
- Big political scandals may follow the mass murder of Afghan war veterans on Sunday.
- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko is set to publicly offer a confederation between his country and Russia when he takes the floor in the Russian Duma on Wednesday.
- President Yeltsin has to unite those people who are nostalgic for the past and those who have started on their way to build a new Russia.

- Settling of accounts between mafia groups and the Afghan war invalids fund or in-fighting within the fund itself are the two main explanations that emerge after Sunday's bomb blast at Kotlyakovskoye cemetery.
